LEGAL SERVICE PiNOY TADA' u PALAUD, DILG Legal Opinion No. 39 s. 2011 JUL 18 MR. EDITO P. GAN 09084550126 Dear Mr. Gan, This refers to your text query on whether it is lawful for the son of a deceased Sangguniang Bayan Member (SB Member) to "take over" the said position as what allegedly happened in Silang, Cavite. Perhaps, due to the means in which you have communicated to us your query, you failed to mention the exact rank of the deceased member in the Sangguniang Bayan. Be that as it may, please be informed that under the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC), if the deceased SB Member is not ranked last in the sanggunian, as may be determined in the results of the immediately preceding local election, then the rule on automatic succession by the other sanggunian members shall be applied first. For instance, if the deceased SB Member is ranked number three (3), the fourth (4th) ranking SB Member shall first be elevated to the third (3rd) rank, and so on with the remaining SB Members. Thereafter, the resultant vacancy in the last position would call for the application of Section 45 of the LGC, which provides in part that permanent vacancies in the sangguniang bayan where automatic succession do not apply shall be filled by appointment to be made by the governor. Furthermore, the same provision provides that the appointee shall come from the same political party as that of the sanggunian member who caused the vacancy and shall serve the unexpired term of the vacant office. On the other hand, if the deceased SB Member is ranked last, then Section 45 of the LGC may at once be applied. Therefore, based on the foregoing, the assumption to office of the son of a deceased Sangguniang Bayan Member would be unlawful if the same is not in accordance with the aforementioned provision of law. Very truly yours, ATT . JESU B.D QUEIV Director 111 14
